findings.description: check_owners.py CODES emits `invalid_registry` and `registry_not_found` (both errors, also documented in SKILL.md and the session log), but the design D9 table in design.md does not list them. The spec's Ownership Check requirement says `code` is 'one of the stable identifiers enumerated in design D9' and task 3.5 asserts 'every emitted code is in the D9 table', so the normative enumeration and the implementation disagree; test_codes_table_has_the_documented_codes only checks a subset relation and so does not catch it.
findings.resolution: Add `invalid_registry` and `registry_not_found` rows to the D9 table (error class) so the design, SKILL.md and CODES enumerate the same contract.

findings.description: tasks.md 5.2 (marked done) says the repository map assigns capabilities `ownership-map` and `agent-identity`, but openspec/owners.yaml assigns `agent-identity` and `agent-coordinator`. The session log records why (`openspec/specs/ownership-map/` does not exist until archival and would trip `unknown_capability`), but the task text was not updated, so the checked-off task no longer describes the delivered artifact.
findings.resolution: Reword 5.2 to name `agent-identity` and `agent-coordinator` and cite the archival reason.

findings.description: The skills-side registry reader validates each `humans:` entry against human-principals.schema.json, but that schema is per-entry; the principal-id slug pattern and 64-char limit live only in the coordinator's AGENTS_SCHEMA `propertyNames`. principals.read_registry therefore accepts an id such as `Jan_N` that load_agents_config() rejects, so the resolver can resolve owners the coordinator will never load. This is the 'reader duplication' risk D2 names, and the pinned schema does not cover it because the key constraint is outside the mirrored dict.
findings.resolution: Check each `humans:` key against the shared slug pattern (and max length) in read_registry and raise `invalid_registry`; add a fixture test with a non-slug id.

findings.description: codeowners.tracked_files calls subprocess.run with timeout=60 but catches nothing; a hung `git ls-files` raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired out of reconcile() and check_owners --codeowners instead of producing a finding. principals._git handles the same failure classes (OSError, SubprocessError) and returns None, so the two git wrappers behave differently on the failure path this module is meant to guard.
findings.resolution: Wrap the run in try/except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) and surface a `not_a_git_checkout` (or new) error finding rather than a traceback.

findings.description: check_owners.check() returns `mode: null` whenever collect_problems yields no context (invalid map, unknown owner, team registry without map), but SKILL.md documents the --json shape with `mode` and the mode contract as `"solo" | "team"` only. Consumers keying on mode will see a third value the contract does not mention.
findings.resolution: Document that `mode` is null when the report carries configuration errors, or emit the derived mode when the registry loaded even if the map failed.

findings.description: The rule-6 human-projection checkers (_strings / _strings_in) test exact string equality against the human id, so a projection that embedded the id in a composite string (e.g. `agent:jan`, a role path `agents/jan/...` or an AppRole name) would not be reported. The negative tests only inject a bare `jan` row, so they do not prove coverage of that shape; the invariant is weaker than the spec's 'no human id appears in any projection' wording.
findings.resolution: Optionally also match the id as a whole token inside longer strings (word-boundary regex) and add a negative test with a composite name; acceptable to defer since no current projection builds composite ids from agent names.

findings.description: test_adding_a_capability_directory_causes_no_unowned_churn asserts `report["findings"] == []` and then asserts no finding code starts with `unowned_`; the second assertion is vacuous after the first and would never fail independently, so the D14-specific intent it documents is not separately exercised.
findings.resolution: Drop the redundant line or run the copy in team mode (two humans) to show the churn probe actually distinguishes unowned_* behaviour.

findings.description: Re-verification of open ledger item 2: proposal.md Selected Approach now reads '(D1–D14)' in the diff, so the range mismatch is resolved and the item can be closed.

Re-verification of open ledger item 6: the PathPattern regex in owners.schema.json (all three copies) still admits an embedded `**`; the loader rejects it (compile_pattern, covered by test_embedded_double_star_rejected and fixture embedded_double_star_schema_ok.json). The two-layer split remains as designed in D3; no change in status.
findings.resolution: Keep open as advisory or close as accepted-by-design.
